prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1189; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a rear-end collision at a signalized intersection. Insured vehicle struck the rear of claimant's vehicle while stopped at a red light. Police report requested. Insured reports sudden braking by claimant, disputes following distance. Photos of both vehicles on file.

Entry 2: Claimant has retained counsel. Representation letter received requesting that all further contact be directed to the attorney's office. Claimant reports wrist fracture sustained in the impact, treated at local emergency department and referred to orthopedic follow-up. Medical authorization requested through counsel.

Entry 3: Spoke with defense liaison regarding liability assessment. Police report reviewed; citation issued to insured driver for following too closely. Witness statement from bystander supports claimant's account of stopping. Liability position leaning toward insured. Reserve reviewed and adjusted to reflect probable bodily injury exposure.

Entry 4: Received orthopedic records through claimant's counsel. Diagnosis confirms closed fracture of the wrist, immobilization in cast, and recommended physical therapy over several weeks. Claimant's counsel submitted itemized medical bills and wage loss documentation. Records forwarded to medical review for evaluation of treatment reasonableness.

Entry 5: Counsel contacted to confirm receipt of medical file and request outstanding employer wage verification. Settlement evaluation scheduled pending completion of medical review. Diary set for follow-up in thirty days. Insured notified of claim status and reminded to forward any correspondence received directly.
